page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. Featuring 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading at 2.6 GHz, the instance delivers predictable per-core execution. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache and 1 MB L2 cache per core, alongside 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB DDR5, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio aligned with standard compute-focused allocations. The system provisions no local instance storage and relies exclusively on remote EBS volumes, while integrating a 200 Gbps network interface baseline for high-throughput distributed operations.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate pronounced throughput across highly parallelized computational workloads. The platform registers top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance (20,928.0) and Clang software compilation (59,549.0), complemented by a strong multi-core stress-ng metric of 97,902.06. Memory subsystem performance is similarly distinguished, scoring in the top decile on PassMark memory evaluations (3,164.24) and sustaining 276.25 GB/s uncached sequential reads and 120.88 GB/s writes. In network and protocol-intensive tasks, it yields 100.31 million Redis SET operations per second and 72.03 GB/s in static web throughput. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as single-core stress-ng (1,532.29) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.93 GB/s) settle in the median range.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and absence of bundled local storage present architectural tradeoffs, necessitating external storage configurations for disk-heavy applications. However, the dedicated core architecture paired with 200 Gbps baseline networking makes c7gn.16xlarge highly cost-efficient for scale-out parallel computing, high-performance web tiering, network virtual appliances, CI/CD build farms, and distributed in-memory data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture operating at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Each core is dedicated without hyperthreading, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance omits local ephemeral storage and features a 200 Gbps network bandwidth baseline without integrated GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates strong parallel execution, evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 20,928.0, top-tier Clang software compilation throughput of 59,549.0, and high memory throughput reaching 276.25 GB/s for uncached reads. Single-threaded metrics remain average, reflecting balanced individual core throughput. The instance delivers high resource efficiency for network-intensive and multithreaded compute tasks, including large-scale CI/CD compilation, distributed caching, network appliances, and static web serving.
